6.0-Magnitude Earthquake Detected Off Coast of Mie Prefecture, Japan

02 Nov 2026, 12:30 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Key takeaways Seismic Activity Reported Near Shima A 6.0-magnitude earthquake occurred off the coast of Japan’s Mie Prefecture early Sunday morning, according to data provided by the United States Geological Survey (USGS). The seismic event was recorded approximately 58 kilometers

Seismic Activity Reported Near Shima

A 6.0-magnitude earthquake occurred off the coast of Japan’s Mie Prefecture early Sunday morning, according to data provided by the United States Geological Survey (USGS). The seismic event was recorded approximately 58 kilometers southeast of the city of Shima and 110 kilometers south-southeast of Tsu, the prefectural capital.

Technical Details

  • Magnitude: 6.0
  • Depth: 352 kilometers
  • Location: Off the coast of Mie Prefecture, Japan
  • Tsunami Risk: No tsunami warning was issued by authorities following the event.

Impact and Observations

While official agencies have not yet released reports regarding infrastructure damage or injuries, residents in the affected region have shared subjective accounts of the tremors. Entries on the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) platform from individuals in the area described the shaking as a prolonged event, noting that the motion began gently before intensifying.

Because of the significant depth of the earthquake, the surface impact may be more localized or less severe than a shallow quake of similar magnitude. Authorities continue to monitor the situation, and further assessments from local disaster management offices are expected.

How to Verify Information

For official updates and verified seismic data, the public is encouraged to consult the following resources:

  • USGS Earthquake Hazards Program: Provides real-time updates and tectonic analysis on global seismic activity.
  • Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA): Issues authoritative information regarding tsunamis, local intensity, and safety protocols for residents in Japan.
  • EMSC (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre): Offers crowdsourced reports and real-time seismic monitoring data.
